channel.title: The Valley Desk
channel.description: Local health-tech news for people and agents

item.title: Jefferson Einstein Philadelphia and Montgomery: MyEinsteinHealth ends Sept. 26, 2026
item.description: After Sept. 26, 2026, patients will no longer access MyEinsteinHealth; records are in MyJeffersonHealth (Epic MyChart) after the next visit to either Einstein hospital, with up to three years of records moved.

item.title: 84 Del. Laws ch. 408, effective Sept. 19, 2024: PBM 340B nondiscrimination
item.description: 84 Del. Laws ch. 408 (HS 1 for HB 383) took effect Sept. 19, 2024 and bars a PBM or purchaser from paying a 340B covered entity less than the CMS NADAC rate, or WAC if NADAC is unavailable.

item.title: ChristianaCare Epic go-live, official July 2026 update
item.description: ChristianaCare’s Oct. 3 Epic cutover is tied to role-based training and readiness checks for caregivers.

item.title: Jefferson FY2026 operating loss and Fitch liquidity
item.description: The $181.5 million year-end operating loss sits next to $5.5 billion / 119 DCOH through March 31; Harrington says the climb holds only if commercial contracts do.

item.title: Penn in-house scribe headcount and 2024 JAMA pilot table
item.description: Penn’s in-house scribe reached roughly 1,200 ambulatory users; a separate 46-clinician DAX Copilot study reported 20.4% less note time per appointment.

item.title: Temple expands Dragon Copilot to 400 end users
item.description: Temple expanded Dragon Copilot to 400 end users after reporting a greater than 10 percent reduction in after-hours documentation during the pilot.

item.title: CHOP publishes ORCA repo
item.description: ORCA is an offline read-only Epic order-set viewer for downtime; it does not hold patient data and cannot place orders.

item.title: Tower Health CIO on AI label, AI tax, and owned platforms
item.description: Tower will not pay an AI premium without a proof-of-value under its own conditions, and it is pressing vendors for value from platforms it already owns.

item.title: Temple Health–Chestnut Hill Hospital and Jefferson Health Plans: contract scheduled to end Sept. 30, 2026
item.description: Temple Health–Chestnut Hill Hospital's contract with Jefferson Health Plans is scheduled to end Sept. 30, 2026, and starting Oct. 1 Jefferson Health Plans would not pay for care there if no new agreement is reached.

item.title: HAP June 10, 2025 letter: enforce CMS-0057-F; 1.6 million Pennsylvanians in Medicare Advantage
item.description: On June 10, 2025, HAP asked CMS to enforce the Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule (CMS-0057-F), citing 1.6 million Pennsylvanians in Medicare Advantage (54 percent of the state's Medicare beneficiaries).

item.title: QGenda QuickLinks showed on-call schedules and clinician cell numbers at Penn, CHOP, and ChristianaCare
item.description: Penn, CHOP, and ChristianaCare pulled public QGenda QuickLinks in late August after the Inquirer showed they displayed on-call schedules and clinician cell numbers without a login; CHOP said the platform holds no patient information.

item.title: Main Line Health cloud analytics
item.description: Main Line Health said Aug. 17 that cloud analytics cut a 30-day wait to near real-time reporting, with 2,017 subscriptions and 6.2 percent monthly access growth since August 2025.

item.title: Benjamin Slovis: Temple Health on Epic’s 2026 Honor Roll
item.description: Temple Health is on Epic’s 2026 Honor Roll; Slovis posted it Aug. 8, and Temple’s July 16 newsroom called the designation Cum Laude and named a $418,000 Epic Good Maintenance grant.
